children: By Jessica Flint | Video and photography by Tina Russell for WSJ

Along Florida's southwest Gulf Coast across Sarasota and Manatee counties, the North Port-Sarasota-Bradenton area is the U.S.'s wealthiest retiree real-estate market, based on total real-estate wealth of homeowners aged 65 and over, according to Realtor.com. The region spans from laid-back Bradenton in the north to rapidly growing North Port in the south. Culture-rich Sarasota is in the middle. "In North Port alone, homeowners 65 and older hold an estimated $102 billion in housing value," says Anthony Smith, a senior economist with Realtor.com. (News Corp, owner of The Wall Street Journal, also operates Realtor.com.) Buyers descend on this area for housing variety, from golf communities and age-qualified enclaves to canal-front single-family homes and master-planned developments equipped for age-in-place living, said Nikki Taylor, a Douglas Elliman real-estate agent.
Old Florida charm at an attainable price point

Bradenton has relaxed coastal living, direct boating waterways and easy access to Anna Maria Island without Sarasota's premium price tag. Its median sale price was $319,778 in October, according to Redfin.
Room to grow in a less-crowded frontier

North Port's median listing sale price was $339,838 in September, according to Redin. It's Sarasota County's largest and fastest-growing city, yet remains only 20% built-out with abundant green buffers. It also has the state's only public warm-water mineral spring and parts of the master-planned hub of Wellen Park, home to the Atlanta Braves spring training complex.
A cultural heavyweight just down the road

With a median listing price of $679,527 in October, according to Redfin, Sarasota serves as the region's arts capital, home to the Ringling museum, the Sarasota Opera and Sarasota Ballet. Residents in neighboring towns can live at a lower price point while remaining an easy 20- to 45-minute drive from a cultural district.
High-net-worth retirees, out-of-state transferees and active seniors. They are seeking warm Gulf Coast winters, availability of healthcare systems and socially active, master-planned communities.

Open-concept floor plans, main-floor primary suites, screened lanais with heated pools and hurricane-impact glass, as well as community access to racquet clubs, fitness centers and neighborhood dining.
Scenic corridors in West Bradenton off Manatee Avenue near Robinson Preserve, alongside amenity-rich avenues winding through Wellen Park communities such as Gran Paradiso.

"Communities across the region are actively doing refreshes, offering savvy buyers an opportunity for entry before improvements lift baseline property values," says Taylor. She recommends prospective buyers meet directly with community representatives to evaluate personal aging-in-place needs, and consult the HOA on upcoming capital-improvement projects.

This contemporary-style custom-build home is in Sarasota's Lakewood Ranch community. Designed by luxury builder John Cannon Homes, the home's design features living space on one level. It has large indoor-outdoor living spaces, including covered lanais and a pool. There is also an outdoor kitchen area. Agent: Evan Grigoli, John Cannon Homes.

This condo was designed for low-maintenance ownership. It's in Sarasota's Rosemary District, close to downtown Sarasota. A floating staircase is a centerpiece. There is a three-stop elevator that provides access from the ground level garage to an upper terrace. It was constructed with concrete and steel, and equipped with impact-rated glass. Agent: Joel Schemmel, J.D., Douglas Elliman.
